10.1002_adma.202514988: Aluminum (Al) foil anodes, alloyed with lithium (Li), offer a theoretical capacity of 993 mAhg −1 and are considered promising candidates for next‐generation high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, their practical application is hindered by non‐uniform alloying processes initiated by the native Al 2 O 3 passivation layer, leading to severe structural degradation and electrode pulverization. Here, a self‐evolving gradient alloy strategy is proposed that enables uniform Li alloying through the in situ construction of a lithiophilic zinc (Zn) interfacial layer on commercial Al foil via a scalable electroless plating process. The Zn interlayer initiates a low‐barrier, sequential alloying pathway—from LiZn to LiAl—thereby promoting uniform lithium infusion, suppressing stress accumulation, and stabilizing the solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI). As a result, the Al@Zn anode achieves an ultralong cycling lifespan with a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.92% over 11 800 cycles, and powers full cells delivering an energy density of 452 Wh kg −1 . Comprehensive structural, electrochemical, and theoretical analyses confirm that the Zn‐guided interfacial gradient effectively mitigates mechanical failure and interfacial instability. This work presents a practical and scalable interfacial engineering approach toward stable, high‐performance alloy‐type anodes, paving the way for the next generation of lithium‐ion batteries.
10.1002_smll.202513812: As a pivotal component in sodium‐metal batteries (SMBs), separators play a crucial role in determining battery electrochemical performance and safety. The development of high‐performance functional separators represents a critical step toward advancing SMBs commercialization. Herein, both the surface chemistry of PAN fibers and the porous structure of the separator are engineered to enhance Na + transport kinetics and optimize Na + deposition on the anode surface through chemical modification and microfibrillation of PAN. The separator features abundant functional groups (─COO − and ─CONH 2 ) and a unique Na + relay mechanism to enhance Na + transport kinetics, while the tailored pore architecture stemming from large numbers of crosslinking microfibrils enables the uniform flux and deposition of Na. The synergistic effect enables the Na//Na symmetric cell to operate stably for 2000 h. Furthermore, the Na//Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cell demonstrates outstanding cycling stability, maintaining 93.7% of its initial capacity after 6000 cycles at 5C. This work establishes a viable pathway for mass‐producing a high‐performance separator for SMBs.
10.1016_j.ijhydene.2026.156063: The global transition toward sustainable energy systems demands advanced technologies capable of achieving substantial reductions in transportation-related emissions. Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) powered electric vehicles represent a compelling pathway; however, their operational performance is highly contingent upon maintaining a stable DC bus voltage, which is inherently challenged by the nonlinear electrochemical behavior of the fuel cell stack and by rapid, unpredictable load fluctuations. In this context, the article proposes a new control architecture for the PEMFC powered DC-DC boost converter, with emphasis on enhancing robustness and efficiency under dynamic operating conditions. The mathematical models and Simulink implementations of the PEMFC stack, the DC-DC converter, and the complete propulsion chain, including an electric vehicle benchmark, are presented. Several control paradigms for maintaining a constant voltage in the intermediate DC bus are comparatively analyzed, including Proportional Integral (PI), Fractional-Order (FO) PI, Sliding Mode Control (SMC), and FOSMC. It also demonstrates the stability and robustness of the FOSMC controller, which provides the best results among the analyzed controllers. Furthermore, an advanced combination of the baseline FOSMC controller with a Machine Learning component is introduced, designed, trained, tested, and implemented as a Reinforcement Learning Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic (RL-TD3) agent that provides real-time adaptive corrections. The tuning parameters of the controllers are optimized using the Beluga Whale Optimization (BWO) metaheuristic algorithm. The Software-In-the-Loop (SIL) results demonstrate the superiority of the FOSMC controller enhanced with the RL-TD3 agent, offering robustness to both parametric variations and load disturbances. In the Hardware-In-the-Loop (HIL) stage, starting from a Matlab/Simulink benchmark, the propulsion chain of a PEMFC powered electric vehicle supplied through a DC bus is further validated, including the implementation of an automatic speed-regulation control at a prescribed reference. This configuration enables Rapid Control Prototyping (RCP) using an OPAL-RT OP4512 real-time platform.
10.1021_acs.analchem.5c05714: Inspired by the color patterns of blue-winged teals' feathers, a new biomimetic imprinting (IM) probe with chemical fluorescent (CF) color and physical structural (PS) color was developed for the label-free and ratiometric detection of levofloxacin (LOF). The probe is defined by a periodic photonic crystal structure formed by monodisperse imprinting microspheres that incorporate LOF-binding nanocavities, similar to the color emission structure of teals. With the increase of the LOF solution, the probe can selectively bind LOF molecules and demonstrate a two-color response without the use of labels: the CF color emerged from the entering of CF color-emissive LOF molecules, further enhanced by the Purcell effect, while the PS color resulted from the periodic photonic crystal structure. As the concentration of LOF increases, the CF color becomes brighter (turn on), while the PS color becomes darker (turn off). These color changes are perceptible to the naked eye. The probe demonstrated label-free, sensitive (down to 2.77 nmol/L), rapid (10 min), selective, and stable detection of the LOF, utilizing a self-correction function of colors. In addition, the probe was successfully applied in real sample detection.
10.1039_d5ta09284a: This study investigates how thermal gradients govern ion transport, reaction kinetics, and morphological stability in sodium metal electrodes by altering thermo-diffusion, SEI interactions, and temperature-dependent mechanics.
10.1039_d6ta00152a: This study integrates Ni and HOF nanorods onto GDY, utilizing its acetylene bonds for substrate adsorption, Ni for electron capture, and HOF for an induced fit microenvironment—a novel strategy for high-performance non-noble-metal photocatalysts.
